promise_positive_consequence_for_complet.definition: A <promise positive consequence for behaviour BCT> in which the consequence will be provided for performing the final behaviour in a sequence of behaviours, followed by adding behaviours that occur earlier in the sequence.

promise_positive_consequence_for_incompa.label: promise positive consequence for incompatible behaviour BCT
promise_positive_consequence_for_incompa.definition: A <promise positive consequence for behaviour BCT> that promises the consequence will be provided for the behaviour that is incompatible with the unwanted behaviour.

promise_positive_consequence_for_outcome.definition: A <promise consequence for outcome of behaviour BCT> where the consequence is positive

promise_positive_consequence_for_situati.label: promise positive consequence for situation specific behaviour BCT

prompt_comparative_imagining_of_future_o.definition: An <increase awareness of consequences BCT> that guides the person to imagine and compare the consequences of performing and not performing the behaviour.

prompt_focus_on_past_success_bct.label: prompt focus on past success BCT
prompt_focus_on_past_success_bct.definition: A <prompt thinking related to successful performance BCT> that prompts the person to think about previous successful performance of the behaviour.

prompt_focus_on_self_identity_bct.label: prompt focus on self-identity BCT
prompt_focus_on_self_identity_bct.definition: A <behaviour change technique> that prompts the person to focus on their mental representation of themself.

prompt_mental_rehearsal_of_successful_pe.label: prompt mental rehearsal of successful performance BCT
prompt_mental_rehearsal_of_successful_pe.definition: A <prompt thinking related to successful performance BCT> that prompts the person to practise imagining performing the behaviour well in a relevant context.

prompt_thinking_related_to_successful_pe.label: prompt thinking related to successful performance BCT

remove_consequence_for_behaviour_bct.definition: A <behavioural consequence BCT> that removes a previously provided consequence for performing the behaviour.

restructure_the_physical_environment_bct.label: restructure the physical environment BCT

restructure_the_social_environment_bct.label: restructure the social environment BCT
restructure_the_social_environment_bct.definition: A <restructure the environment BCT> that alters the social environment in which the behaviour is, or would have been, performed in a way that facilitates or impedes the behaviour.

review_behaviour_goal_bct.definition: A <goal directed BCT> that reviews a behavioural goal and considers modifying the goal in light of progress toward the goal.

review_behaviour_goal_plan_bct.label: review behaviour goal plan BCT
review_behaviour_goal_plan_bct.definition: A <goal directed BCT> that reviews progress towards a behavioural goal and considers modifying the plan to achieve the goal.

review_outcome_goal_bct.label: review outcome goal BCT
review_outcome_goal_bct.definition: A <goal directed BCT> that reviews an outcome goal and considers modifying the goal in light of achievement.

self_monitor_behaviour_bct.label: self-monitor behaviour BCT
self_monitor_behaviour_bct.definition: A <monitoring BCT> in which the person uses a method to monitor and record their behaviour.

self_monitor_outcome_of_behaviour_bct.label: self-monitor outcome of behaviour BCT
self_monitor_outcome_of_behaviour_bct.definition: A <monitoring BCT> in which the person uses a method to monitor and record an outcome of their behaviour.

set_behaviour_goal_bct.definition: A <goal setting BCT> that sets a goal for the behaviour to be achieved.

set_graded_tasks_bct.label: set graded tasks BCT
set_graded_tasks_bct.definition: A <goal directed BCT> that sets easy-to-perform tasks for the person, making them increasingly difficult, but achievable, until the behaviour is performed.

set_measurable_behaviour_goal_bct.label: set measurable behaviour goal BCT
set_measurable_behaviour_goal_bct.definition: A <set behaviour goal BCT> that describes the behaviour to be achieved in terms of a measurable target.

set_measurable_outcome_goal_bct.label: set measurable outcome goal BCT
set_measurable_outcome_goal_bct.definition: A <set outcome goal BCT> that describes the behavioural outcome to be achieved in terms of a measurable target.

set_outcome_goal_bct.label: set outcome goal BCT
set_outcome_goal_bct.definition: A <goal setting BCT> in which the goal is a positive outcome of performing the behaviour.

social_support_bct.label: social support BCT
social_support_bct.definition: A <behaviour change technique> that involves taking steps to secure or deliver the support or aid of another person.

substitute_behaviour_bct.label: substitute behaviour BCT
substitute_behaviour_bct.definition: An <advise specific behaviour BCT> that advises the person to replace the unwanted behaviour with another behaviour.

suggest_different_perspective_on_behavio.label: suggest different perspective on behaviour BCT
suggest_different_perspective_on_behavio.definition: A <behaviour change technique> that suggests the deliberate adoption of a new perspective on the behaviour.

suggest_how_to_perform_behaviour_bct.label: suggest how to perform behaviour BCT
suggest_how_to_perform_behaviour_bct.definition: A <guide how to perform behaviour BCT> that provides a suggestion regarding how to perform the behaviour.

suggest_to_change_behaviour_bct.label: suggest to change behaviour BCT
suggest_to_change_behaviour_bct.definition: An <awareness of other people's thoughts, feelings and actions BCT> that involves sharing a view about what behaviour the person should do.

systematically_desensitise_bct.label: systematically desensitise BCT
systematically_desensitise_bct.definition: An <expose to stimulus BCT> that gradually exposes the person to an aversive stimulus while also engaging them in a relaxation process to reduce the response to that stimulus.

tell_to_change_behaviour_bct.label: tell to change behaviour BCT
tell_to_change_behaviour_bct.definition: An <awareness of other people's thoughts, feelings and actions BCT> that involves telling the person to perform the behaviour.

vicarious_punishment_bct.label: vicarious punishment BCT
vicarious_punishment_bct.definition: An <increase awareness of consequences BCT> that prompts observation of another person being punished when they perform the behaviour.

vicarious_reward_bct.label: vicarious reward BCT
vicarious_reward_bct.definition: An <increase awareness of consequences BCT> that prompts observation of another person being rewarded when they perform the behaviour.

amotivation.label: amotivation (SDT regulation)
amotivation.definition: SDT 'amotivation' — the lack of intention to act on a behaviour.

external_regulation.label: behavioural opportunity
external_regulation.definition: SDT 'external regulation' — acting to obtain rewards or avoid punishment.

introjected_regulation.label: introjected self-regulation
introjected_regulation.definition: SDT 'introjected regulation' — acting to avoid guilt or for ego.

identified_regulation.label: accepting responsibility for changing one's behaviour
identified_regulation.definition: SDT 'identified regulation' — acting because the behaviour is personally valued.

intrinsic_motivation.label: intrinsic motivation
intrinsic_motivation.definition: SDT 'intrinsic motivation' — acting for the inherent enjoyment of the behaviour.

autonomous_motivation.label: autonomous motivation
autonomous_motivation.definition: SDT 'autonomous motivation' umbrella — identified + integrated + intrinsic.

default.label: default-based delivery
default.definition: The recommendation pre-selects the desired option so the user receives the healthy choice unless they actively change it (opt-out structure). Use when the task is a one-shot substitution / setting / swap where flipping the default is the mechanism (Bergram et al. 2022, §4.1).

reinforcement.label: reinforcement-based delivery
reinforcement.definition: The recommendation increases salience of the desired behaviour via repetition, priming, anchoring, or persistent cues. Use when the task relies on rehearsal, visible reminders, or accumulated exposure rather than a single point-of-decision intervention (Bergram et al. 2022, §4.1).

social.label: social-norm delivery
social.definition: The recommendation surfaces how peers / family / community behave, leveraging social proof or interpersonal accountability. Use when the task involves another person, comparison with a reference group, or coordinated action (Bergram et al. 2022, §4.1).

disclosure.label: disclosure-based delivery
disclosure.definition: The recommendation surfaces accessible, clear, relevant information at the point of choice (labels, ingredients, calories, caffeine, environmental impact). Use when the task asks the user to inspect / read / verify information before deciding (Bergram et al. 2022, §4.1).

friction.label: friction-based delivery
friction.definition: The recommendation adds or removes effort to discourage or encourage a behaviour. Remove friction by pre-positioning cues (carry bottle, set out gear); add friction against an unwanted behaviour (charge phone outside bedroom, block sites). Use when the mechanism is environment / effort restructuring (Bergram et al. 2022, §4.1).

decoy_deception.label: decoy / deception delivery
decoy_deception.definition: The recommendation covertly affects perception via decoy options or framing manipulation. Rarely appropriate for self-help / behaviour-change recommendations because it conflicts with autonomy and informed consent (Bergram et al. 2022, §4.1).

feedback.label: feedback-based delivery
feedback.definition: The recommendation provides information about a past or current behaviour (eco-score, step count, mood after a session). Use when the task asks the user to log, track, mark, or reflect on what they just did (Bergram et al. 2022, §4.1).

warning.label: warning-based delivery
warning.definition: The recommendation grabs attention to a risk or consequence so the user reconsiders the choice. Use when the task surfaces a barrier, a sensitive situation, or a chance to draw a boundary (Bergram et al. 2022, §4.1).

scarcity.label: scarcity-based delivery
scarcity.definition: The recommendation frames the option as scarce in time or quantity ("only one room left", "last 5 minutes"). Use when the task itself relies on a limited window (a seasonal food, a one-day-only event, a today-only commitment) (Bergram et al. 2022, §4.1).

commitment.label: commitment-based delivery
commitment.definition: The recommendation elicits an explicit advance commitment so the user is motivated to act consistently with it (preselecting which household devices to save energy on, signing a pledge, planning the act before the moment of temptation). Use when the task is a deliberate, written or stated, future-oriented commitment (Bergram et al. 2022, §4.1).
